title: World leaders congratulate Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on completion of 25 years as Head of Government
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 OCT 2026 4:56PM by PIB Delhi
content:
World leaders from across continents have extended their warmest greetings and hearty congratulations to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on completing a historic milestone of 25 continuous years as Head of Government on October 7, 2026. Marking twenty five years since he first assumed office as Chief Minister of Gujarat in 2001 and subsequently taking over as the Prime Minister of the Republic of India in 2014, global leaders highlighted his transformative leadership, dedication to good governance, and commitment to global peace, inclusivity, and sustainable development.
Prime Minister of Bhutan, H.E. Tshering Tobgay, congratulated the Prime Minister on this historic milestone. Sharing a letter, he noted that enlightened leadership is the exercise of wisdom, compassion, and courage through selfless service, qualities he sees coming together most clearly in PM Modi's vision of Viksit Bharat. Emphasizing that this vision reflects the collective ambition of 1.4 billion Indians for a strong, prosperous, and developed country, he posted on X;
"To Prime Minister @narendramodi, An avatar of our times

— Tshering Tobgay (@tsheringtobgay)
October 7, 2026
President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, H.E. Bola Ahmed Tinubu, extended warm and fraternal congratulations to PM Modi. Highlighting the visionary leadership that steered the transformation of Gujarat and facilitated India's rise as one of the fastest growing global economies, he shared on X;
"On behalf of the Government and people of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, and on my own behalf, I extend warm and fraternal congratulations to His Excellency Shri Narendra Modi @narendramodi, Prime Minister of the Republic of India, on a truly historic milestone.
Today, 7 October 2026, marks 25 years since he first assumed office in 2001 as Head of Government and Chief Minister of Gujarat.
His public service has continued without interruption. After more than twelve years serving the people of Gujarat, he has remained Prime Minister of the Republic of India since 2014.
A quarter-century of unbroken leadership is a rare achievement in any democracy. In the world's most populous nation, it is a powerful testament to the enduring confidence the Indian people have placed in him.
Across these 25 years, Prime Minister Modi has led with vision and an unwavering commitment to development. From the transformation of Gujarat to India's emergence as one of the world's largest and fastest-growing economies, his leadership in infrastructure, digital public goods, financial inclusion and innovation has lifted millions and inspired nations across the Global South.
Nigeria deeply values the strategic partnership between our two great nations. I fondly recall the Prime Minister's historic State Visit to Abuja in November 2024, when Nigeria honoured him with the title of Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger.
That visit gave fresh impetus to our cooperation in trade and investment, energy, defence and security, health, education, and technology.
As fellow democracies and leading voices of the Global South, Nigeria and India share a common commitment to a fairer, more inclusive and more representative international order. I remain confident that, under his continued leadership, the bonds of friendship between our peoples will grow ever stronger.
As Prime Minister Modi marks this remarkable anniversary, I wish him good health, continued strength and every success in the service of the people of India.
Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR
President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces
Federal Republic of Nigeria
Abuja, 7 October 2026"

title: PM to inaugurate 10th edition of India Mobile Congress on 8 October
subtitle:
Theme of IMC 2026: “Scale Without Boundaries”

Four key Pillars of IMC 2026 - Srishti: Building the Future; Samvardhan: Fueling Growth; Sashakt: Expanding Opportunities; and Suraksha: Strengthening Trust

IMC 2026 to focus on new domains of Smart Mobility, Stadium Experiences, Industrial Robotics and Transport Technology

IMC 2026 to witness participation from over 100 countries
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 OCT 2026 12:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will inaugurate the 10th edition of the India Mobile Congress (IMC) on 8 October 2026 at around 10 AM at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.
Organised jointly by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) and the Cellular Operators Association of India (COAI), the event will be held from 7 to 10 October. The theme of IMC 2026 is “Scale Without Boundaries”, reflecting India’s growing capabilities in digital innovation, next-generation connectivity and technology-led growth.
The four key pillars of IMC 2026 will be - Srishti: Building the Future; Samvardhan: Fueling Growth; Sashakt: Expanding Opportunities; and Suraksha: Strengthening Trust. It will focus on innovation and next-generation digital infrastructure, technology-led economic growth, inclusive digital access, and the development of secure and resilient digital ecosystems. IMC 2026 will bring together global technology leaders, policymakers, industry experts, startups, investors and innovators to explore emerging opportunities across the digital ecosystem
The 2026 edition will cover nine established anchor sectors, including 5G and 6G, next-generation AI networks, semiconductors, non-terrestrial networks, cyber security, quantum communication, enterprise transformation, circular economy and ESG, and electronics manufacturing. The event will also expand its sectoral focus to four new domains - smart mobility, stadium experiences, industrial robotics and transport technology.
IMC 2026 is expected to attract more than 1.5 lakh attendees from over 100 countries, with participation from 500+ partners and exhibitors, 600+ startups and 900+ thought leaders. The event will feature more than 2,000 technology use cases and over 120 sessions.

date:

content:
New Delhi; 7 October, 2026
: Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla paid floral tributes to former Speaker, Lok Sabha, Shri Bali Ram Bhagat, at his portrait in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan on his Birth Anniversary, today.
Secretary-General, Lok Sabha, Shri Utpal Kumar Singh also paid tributes to Shri Bhagat.
A veteran freedom fighter with rich parliamentary experience and deep knowledge of parliamentary practices and procedures, Shri Bhagat was elected as the Speaker of the Fifth Lok Sabha on 5 January 1976. He was a Member of the Provisional Parliament and First, Second, Third, Fourth, Fifth, Seventh and Eighth Lok Sabhas.
As a Union Minister, he held important portfolios, including Finance, Planning, Defence, External Affairs, Foreign Trade and Supply, Steel and Heavy
Engineering. He functioned as the Governor of Himachal Pradesh from February
1993 for four months and Governor of Rajasthan from 30 June 1993 till 1 May 1998.
Shri Bali Ram Bhagat passed away in New Delhi on 2 January 2011.
लोक सभा के पूर्व अध्यक्ष एवं राजस्थान के राज्यपाल रहे स्व. श्री बलि राम भगत जी की जयंती पर संविधान सदन के केंद्रीय कक्ष में भावपूर्ण श्रद्धासुमन अर्पित किए।
श्री बलि राम भगत का सार्वजनिक जीवन स्वतंत्रता संग्राम, संसदीय लोकतंत्र, प्रशासन और सामाजिक सरोकार की एक लंबी एवं बहुआयामी यात्रा रहा। करीब चार दशकों के विधायी जीवन के साथ श्री बलि राम भगत ने संसदीय लोकतंत्र को मजबूत करने में उल्लेखनीय भूमिका निभाई।

वर्ष 1950 में वे Provisional Parliament के लिए निर्वाचित हुए। इसके बाद पहली से पाँचवीं लोक सभा तक 1952 से 1977 के बीच और फिर सातवीं तथा आठवीं लोक सभा में 1980 से 1989 तक संसद के सदस्य रहे। उन्होंने सात बार लोक सभा का प्रतिनिधित्व किया।
5 जनवरी 1976 को श्री बलि राम भगत पाँचवीं लोक सभा के अध्यक्ष निर्वाचित हुए। यह उनके संसदीय जीवन का एक महत्वपूर्ण पड़ाव था। अध्यक्ष पद संभालते समय उन्होंने स्पष्ट रूप से कहा कि Speaker सदन का servant होता है और सदन के सभी वर्गों से समान रूप से संबंधित होता है। उन्होंने अपने दायित्वों को impartiality और निष्पक्षता के साथ निभाने की प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त की।
उनकी अध्यक्षीय कार्यशैली में संसदीय प्रक्रियाओं की गहरी समझ, संयम और व्यवस्था के प्रति दृढ़ प्रतिबद्धता दिखाई दी। उनकी parliamentary skill, procedural knowledge, insight तथा holistic vision के कारण सदन के विभिन्न वर्गों में उनके प्रति सम्मान था।

श्री भगत संसदीय अनुशासन और सदन की मर्यादा को लेकर अत्यंत सजग थे। वे Parliamentary traditions और propriety के दृढ़ समर्थक थे। वे मानते थे कि संसदीय कार्यवाही प्रभावी तभी हो सकती है जब नियमों, समय और प्रक्रियाओं का सम्मान किया जाए। उनकी अध्यक्षीय कार्यशैली में यह विशेष रूप से दिखाई देता था कि कठिन परिस्थितियों में भी वे शांत और संयमित रहते हुए सदन के नियमों का पालन सुनिश्चित करने का प्रयास करते थे।

श्री बलि राम भगत की संसदीय विरासत का एक महत्वपूर्ण पहलू उनकी institution-building approach थी। मार्च 1976 में उनके अध्यक्षीय कार्यकाल के दौरान Committee of Chairmen on Government Assurances का पहला सम्मेलन आयोजित हुआ। उन्होंने इस बात पर जोर दिया कि सदन के पटल पर सरकार द्वारा दिए गए आश्वासनों का उचित रूप से पालन और कार्यान्वयन सुनिश्चित होना चाहिए।
इसी वर्ष Parliamentary Research and Training Institute for Democracies/PRIDE (Erstwhile BPST) की स्थापना हुई, जो आज लोक सभा सचिवालय का एक महत्वपूर्ण अंग है। संसदीय अध्ययन और प्रशिक्षण की यह पहल जनप्रतिनिधियों तथा संसदीय कार्य से जुड़े लोगों के लिए क्षमता निर्माण की दिशा में महत्वपूर्ण कदम थी।
यह उनकी उस सोच को दर्शाता है जिसमें संसद को केवल बहस और कानून निर्माण का मंच नहीं, बल्कि ज्ञान, प्रशिक्षण, प्रक्रियागत दक्षता और संस्थागत क्षमता से मजबूत होने वाली लोकतांत्रिक संस्था के रूप में देखा गया।

श्री बलि राम भगत जी का जीवन स्वतंत्रता आंदोलन से शुरू होकर स्वतंत्र भारत की लोकतांत्रिक संस्थाओं के विकास के लिए समर्पित रहा। वे राजस्थान और हिमाचल प्रदेश के राज्यपाल तथा केंद्रीय विदेश मंत्री के पद पर भी रहे। उन्होंने स्वतंत्रता के लिए संघर्ष किया, संसद में जनता का प्रतिनिधित्व किया, केंद्र सरकार में विदेश मंत्री के रूप में महत्वपूर्ण ज़िम्मेदारी निभाईं तथा लोक सभा अध्यक्ष के रूप में संसदीय मर्यादा और प्रक्रियाओं को महत्व दिया।
श्री बलि राम भगत जी की संसदीय विरासत, लोकतांत्रिक प्रतिबद्धता, सामाजिक सरोकार और राष्ट्रसेवा की भावना आने वाली पीढ़ियों के लिए सदैव प्रेरणा का स्रोत बनी रहेगी।

The National Institute of Naturopathy (NIN), Ministry of Ayush, Government of India, has invited applications for admission to the Bachelor of Naturopathy and Yogic Sciences (BNYS) programme for the academic session 2026–27 at its flagship Nisarg Gram campus, Yewalewadi, Pune.
NIN, an autonomous organisation under the Ministry of Ayush, is carrying forward the legacy and vision of Mahatma Gandhi by promoting Naturopathy and Yoga through healthcare, education, training and research. NIN is the first Central Government institution in the country to offer the BNYS programme in affiliation with a Central University, Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University, New Delhi. This marks a significant milestone in strengthening institutional education and academic standards in Naturopathy and Yoga.
The 5½-year full-time residential BNYS programme comprises 4½ years of academic and clinical training, followed by one year of Compulsory Rotatory Residential Internship (CRRI). The programme offers integrated academic education along with extensive clinical exposure in Naturopathy and Yoga. A total of 100 seats are being offered for the academic session 2026–27.
Candidates who have passed 10+2 or an equivalent examination with Physics, Chemistry, Biology (PCB) and English from a recognised Board and fulfil the prescribed eligibility and medical fitness requirements are eligible to apply. Preference will be given to candidates who have appeared for NEET-UG 2026. Any remaining vacant seats will be filled on the basis of 10+2 PCB merit, in accordance with the prescribed admission procedure and reservation norms.
The flagship Nisarg Gram campus, spread over 25 acres, houses a 250-bedded Naturopathy Hospital, academic and research facilities, separate residential hostels for boys and girls, state-of-the-art yoga halls and modern Naturopathy treatment infrastructure. The campus provides an integrated environment for education, clinical training, research and wellness.
The online application process commenced on 29 September 2026 and will close on 19 October 2026 at 5:00 PM. The provisional merit list is scheduled to be released on 27 October 2026, followed by the final merit/waiting list on 30 October 2026. Counselling is scheduled to be conducted on 12–13 November and 18–19 November 2026, while classes are scheduled to commence from 30 November 2026.

title: India and Ghana Sign Historic MoU to Advance Agricultural Research, Education, and Technology Transfer
subtitle: ICAR and CSIR-CRI (Ghana) partner to boost crop yields, post-harvest infrastructure, and commercialization; ceremony graced by External Affairs Ministers of both nations
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 OCT 2026 6:04PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India and Ghana have strengthened cooperation in agricultural research, education and technology transfer with the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), New Delhi, and the Crops Research Institute (CSIR-CRI), Accra, Ghana. This MoU will strengthen India’s focus on South-South and India-Africa collaboration. The signing ceremony was graced by Dr. S. Jaishankar, External Affairs Minister of India, and H.E. Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Minister for Foreign Affairs of Ghana.
The five-year MoU provides a framework for cooperation in joint agricultural research, scientific and technological exchange, capacity building and the application and commercialisation of agricultural technologies. The collaboration has been facilitated by Arima Farms Ltd., Ghana, which has been recognised as the commercial partner to CSIR-CRI for specific research and commercialisation activities under the framework.
The first phase of cooperation will focus on vegetable crop research, with particular emphasis on tomato research and development. Under the collaboration, ICAR will support the scaling up of proven agricultural technologies and the introduction of suitable high-yielding tomato lines and varieties to contribute to strengthening domestic tomato production in Ghana.
The partnership will also focus on processing and value addition of cassava, yam and other tuber crops, with the objective of strengthening agricultural value chains. Cooperation will further cover post-harvest management, including technical support and capacity building in cold storage, refrigerated transportation, sorting, grading and processing technologies, aimed at addressing post-harvest losses.
The MoU provides for exchange of scientists and technologists, germplasm and breeding materials, scientific information, methodologies and technical knowledge, besides development and implementation of collaborative research projects. It also envisages institutional linkages between relevant research institutes and centres of the two countries to facilitate sustained scientific cooperation.
The collaboration will be overseen through a Joint Working Group comprising representatives of ICAR and CSIR-CRI, which will review the progress of cooperation and guide implementation. The Joint Working Group will meet periodically in New Delhi and Accra.
The partnership is expected to strengthen the linkage between agricultural research, technology development, capacity building and commercial application, facilitating the adoption of relevant agricultural technologies and contributing to sustainable agricultural development and improved livelihoods in Ghana.

title: Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal Calls for Greater Utilisation of India-EFTA TEPA Opportunities
subtitle: India-EFTA TEPA Provides Wide Market Access with 99.6% of India’s Exports Covered: Commerce Secretary
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 OCT 2026 4:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal delivered the keynote address to Export Promotion Councils, industry associations and exporters, as well as representatives of business from the EFTA States, at the Outreach Event for Major Exporters to promote utilisation of opportunities under the India-European Free Trade Association (EFTA) Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) in New Delhi, today. The event formed part of the 2nd India-EFTA Prosperity Summit 2026 and was organised by the Department of Commerce.
TEPA entered into force on 1 October 2025. Shri Agrawal said that leaders from all four EFTA States — Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland — are in New Delhi to mark the first year of the Agreement and to guide the way forward.
Shri Agrawal said that India and the EFTA States have opened their markets to each other. EFTA's commitments cover 92.2 per cent of its tariff lines, accounting for 99.6 per cent of India's exports, with full coverage of non-agricultural products. India's commitments cover 82.7 per cent of tariff lines, accounting for 95.3 per cent of EFTA exports.
The Commerce Secretary said that the Agreement is not only about tariffs. Its most important element for business is predictability. Tariffs will remain stable for the foreseeable future, with no surprises. Businesses can therefore make investments, build supply chains and plan for the future with confidence. He urged Indian companies to partner with businesses in the EFTA States and build value chains together, from inputs to final products, for greater reliability on both sides.
Shri Agrawal said that the EFTA States are high-income markets that demand quality and value it. "If you are able to create quality products in this market, then you are ready for any other market," he said. Quality earned in these markets will be appreciated and valued in every market.
He said that agriculture also has a large export opportunity in these high-consumption markets, where duties on many products have come down to zero. Exporters should identify these products and build long-term supply to the EFTA States.
The Commerce Secretary said that the EFTA States together import goods and services worth over half a trillion US dollars a year and this provides an important market for India's exports.
Shri Agrawal called on the Export Promotion Councils, industry associations and State Governments to take the opportunities of the Agreement to businesses in every part of the country, so that they understand what a free trade agreement offers. He asked them to prepare an action plan with each partner country for each market for the next five years, setting out how India will grow in each market and the non-tariff issues to be addressed.
"The idea is not that businesses in EFTA countries only see India as an extension of their market. The idea is also that businesses in India should see the market of EFTA countries as an extension of their market," he said.
The Commerce Secretary said that a key feature that sets TEPA apart from other agreements is its investment commitment. Under Article 7.1 of the Agreement, "the EFTA States shall aim to increase foreign direct investment from investors of the EFTA States into India by 50 billion (US dollars) within 10 years from the entry into force of this Agreement and an additional 50 billion (US dollars) in the succeeding 5 years", and "shall aim to facilitate the generation of 1 million jobs within 15 years in India".
Shri Agrawal said that India is a growing market with investment opportunities across sectors, and that deeper business partnerships on both sides can take investment beyond this level.

Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia attended the interaction along with Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development Dr. Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar and senior officials of the Government of India.
Prime Minister emphasised that technology must become a tool for inclusive and sustainable development. He stressed that democratisation of technology is essential to ensure that no section of society is left behind. He underlined the need to make technology and digital services affordable and accessible, particularly for the Global South, and highlighted the importance of taking technology to the last mile to prevent a widening digital divide.
Prime Minister highlighted the potential of Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) as a transformative force, particularly for developing countries. He noted that discussions on DPI with several world leaders had demonstrated its growing global relevance and said that such platforms can serve as a springboard for countries of the Global South.
Addressing the growing challenge of digital and cyber fraud, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi said the problem requires technology-driven solutions. He suggested sustained awareness messages for users to warn people about potential fraud calls.
Prime Minister also highlighted the need for global standards and common rules for emerging technologies. On the growing threat of deepfakes and AI-generated content, he suggested exploring mechanisms to allow users to immediately identify its origin.
GSMA Board members recognise India’s digital transformation
GSMA Board members highlighted India’s emergence as a global leader in digital and mobile connectivity. They noted the rapid expansion of 4G and 5G, the scale of Digital Public Infrastructure and the growth of India’s telecom and mobile manufacturing ecosystem.
They appreciated India’s investment-friendly policy framework and emphasised the role of secure, resilient and trusted digital infrastructure in supporting continued digital growth.
The Board members also highlighted growing opportunities for international cooperation with India in areas including 5G, 6G, AI, cybersecurity, digital inclusion and satellite connectivity.
Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia’s global telecom engagement strengthens India’s technology partnerships
The interaction comes as India prepares to host the 10th edition of the India Mobile Congress, bringing together global technology and telecom leaders in New Delhi.
Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia has been leading India’s international engagement on next-generation connectivity and digital technologies. At Mobile World Congress 2026 in Barcelona, he led India’s engagements with the global telecom ecosystem and addressed the GSMA Ministerial Programme on making connectivity more affordable, inclusive and future-ready.
India’s engagement with global technology leaders reflects the country’s growing role in shaping the future of telecommunications, including the evolution of 6G, secure digital infrastructure, Artificial Intelligence and globally interoperable technology standards.
With India increasingly contributing to global conversations on next-generation connectivity and digital public infrastructure, the interaction with the GSMA Board further strengthens India’s partnerships with the global mobile ecosystem.

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Balasore City under OD LSA, during the month of August 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), data Download (DL) and Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services.
These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc. In this type of drive testing, live data and voice sessions are established using SIM cards from all TSPs over 2G, 3G, 4G, and 5G networks. Multiple advanced test handsets are used, and the sessions are monitored and analysed in real-time using advanced Software Systems.
TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests across City drive – 345 Kms, Hotspot locations - 7, in Balasore city during 18th August 2026 to 20th August 2026 in Odisha LSA
.
These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Hyderabad. The observations presented in drive test reports represent the performance of the TSPs on the area/ route under test on the day/ time of conducting the drive test.

Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less than the minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 4G/ 5G).
Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, Call Silence Rate, Speech Quality (MOS).

Data Servies: Download/ Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate

title: Adequate availability of Onion at affordable prices in the country
subtitle:
Fresh Kharif Onion arrivals gain momentum;

Onion mandi and retail prices show broad-based moderation across the country

Buffer stock disposal expanded to 123 cities, with 8 Kanda Express and 467 trucks

Government expands Calibrated and strategic release of buffer onion
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 OCT 2026 5:57PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Onion Availability and Kharif Onion Scenario
The outlook for onion availability has strengthened considerably, with
higher Kharif acreage, favorable crop conditions, robust market arrivals and the commencement of fresh Kharif supplies
supporting the market. The improving supply position is already translating into a broad-based moderation in onion prices across mandis and major consumer markets.
Fresh Kharif onion arrivals have commenced from major producing States, including
Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan
, while availability from stored stocks continues to meet market demands. Arrivals from these producing regions are expected to increase further in the coming weeks, improving overall availability in the consuming markets during upcoming festive season.
The production outlook for the Kharif crop is encouraging.
All-India Kharif onion acreage is estimated to be around 5 per cent higher than last year's already strong level
, with crop conditions remaining favourable across major producing regions. The rainfall outlook by IMD during the harvesting period also provides support to the crop, with no forecast of excessive rains in key Kharif onion regions in coming weeks to facilitate harvesting, drying and movement of onions and reduce the risk of moisture-related crop damage.
Onion mandi price scenario in Maharashtra
The strengthening supply situation is being reflected in mandi prices. Arrivals across key onion markets have remained robust, with the
weighted average mandi price in Maharashtra declining by nearly 13 per cent
, from around
₹4,030 per quintal on 16 September to about ₹3,475 per quintal on 3 October
. The sustained moderation in mandi prices indicates that the increase in market arrivals is translating into improved supply conditions.
Onion Retail Price Scenario
The easing trend is also visible across retail markets.
126 cities have reported a decline of ₹1–21 per kg in retail onion prices over the past two weeks
, with moderation observed in major consuming States including
Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal
. The broad-based nature of the decline across geographically dispersed markets indicates that the improvement is not confined to individual mandis or regions but reflects strengthening availability across the country.
Strategic Release of Government Buffer Stock
The Government is also augmenting supplies to consuming centres through
buffer stock release. As on date, the government has disposed off more than 2.0 lakh Quintals through 8 Kanda Express and 467 trucks across 123 cities and is planning to deploy additional rail rakes
, enabling larger quantities of onions to reach high-consumption markets. These efforts are being further strengthened ahead of the festive season, with additional rail movements being planned to improve the speed and efficiency of supply distribution.
The combination of
fresh Kharif arrivals, availability from stored stocks and continued movement of buffer onions to consumption centres
provides multiple channels of supply to the market. The Government is maintaining close oversight of arrivals, stocks and price movements and is taking appropriate measures to facilitate orderly distribution and adequate availability wherever required.
Overall,
higher Kharif acreage, favourable crop conditions, conducive harvesting weather, robust arrivals and a broad-based decline in mandi and retail prices point to a comfortable onion availability outlook in the coming weeks
. With fresh Kharif Onion supplies expected to gain further momentum and Government distribution efforts being strengthened ahead of the festive season, the supply position is expected to remain well supported and prices will further moderate.

content:
An ancient metal-casting tradition takes centre stage in a collection of 16 mementos from Chhattisgarh, bringing together the state’s rich tribal heritage, devotional traditions and contemporary cultural identity.
At the heart of the collection is Dhokra, the traditional lost-wax metal-casting craft having a history of more than 4,000 years in India. Several Dhokra works showcase the distinctive character and versatility of the tradition, including an Elephant Head Nandi, Standing Nandi and Madia-Madin Tribal Couple Bust.
The story of tribal Chhattisgarh continues through a traditional ceremonial headgear featuring a peacock-feather cluster, cowrie shells, metallic discs and brass bells.
Beyond tribal craft, the collection brings together the many cultural influences that shape the state. A Ramnami Samaj chanting stole, covered with repeated inscriptions of “Ram Ram”, represents a distinctive expression of faith and devotion. Other mementos depict important religious and cultural landmarks, including Hatkeshwar Mahadev, Budeshwar Mahadev, Jai Maa Kudargadi and Madheshwar Mahadev.
The collection also captures a more contemporary Chhattisgarh. A woodcut panel depicting the Mahtari Vandan Yojana, a memento marking the Rajat Jayanti of the Chhattisgarh Vidhan Sabha, and models representing institutions in Nava Raipur reflect the state’s evolving present alongside its traditional heritage.
The collection’s central message is one of continuity. Traditions that have been shaped over generations continue to find expression in contemporary objects, carrying the cultural memory of Chhattisgarh forward.

content:
Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth inaugurated the Multinational Search and Rescue Exercise (SAREX-2026) on October 07, 2026, set to be conducted off Paradip on October 08, 2026. The exercise will witness the participation and observation of 32 delegates from 30 foreign friendly nations.
Addressing the gathering, RRM welcomed the representatives of international organisations and friendly foreign countries and appreciated their presence as the mutual commitment towards enhancing cooperation and strengthening maritime safety across the region. He said the participation of the Navy, Coast Guard, Air Force, Coastal Police, Ports, Civil Agencies, Shipping Community and international and regional partners demonstrates that modern maritime security is not the responsibility of any single agency, but requires a Whole-of-Government and Whole-of-Nation approach.
The Raksha Rajya Mantri highlighted India's continued efforts to strengthen its Search and Rescue capabilities through cooperation, preparedness and technological advancement. He noted that India's journey in Satellite Aided Search and Rescue has progressively evolved from Low Earth Orbit Search and Rescue (LEOSAR) to Geostationary Search and Rescue (GEOSAR) and now towards Medium Earth Orbit Search and Rescue (MEOSAR). He described the achievement of full operations capability of the Indian Earth Orbit Local User Terminal (MEOLUT) as a significant advancement in India's satellite-aided Search and Rescue capability. RRM congratulated ISRO and all associated teams for the achievement and their contribution towards strengthening India's national Search and Rescue (SAR) capabilities.
The Raksha Rajya Mantri called upon all participating agencies and international partners to reaffirm their shared commitment to safeguarding lives at sea and to strengthen the spirit of cooperation that underpins effective Search and Rescue across the region. Invoking the principle of ‘One Earth, One Family, One Future’, he said collective efforts can build a safer, more resilient and more cooperative maritime community.
Shri Seth emphasised that as India moves towards the aspirations of Viksit Bharat 2047, its SAR capabilities must evolve, becoming faster, accurate and more resilient. He said a developed and empowered India must also become a safe, resilient and technologically advanced maritime nation, as reflected meaningfully in the motto of the Indian Coast Guard - Vayam Rakshamah (We Protect).”
SAREX-2026 is a multi-agency exercise aimed at validating operational preparedness, enhancing international interoperability, testing joint response mechanisms and fostering the exchange of best practices, with preservation of life at sea as the paramount objective of every mission.
The 24th National Maritime Search and Rescue (NMSAR) Board Meeting was also convened earlier today under the chairmanship of Director General Paramesh Sivamani, DG Indian Coast Guard and Chairman, NMSAR Board on October 07, 2026. The board reviewed the preparedness of maritime Search and Rescue operations across the 4.6 million sq km Indian Search & Rescue Region (ISRR). During the meeting, deliberations were held on technological integration, real-time information sharing, distress-alert management, vessel tracking and inter-agency coordination, providing the operational foundation for SAREX-2026.     The Chairman underscored that operational lessons derived from past missions and multi-agency exercises must directly translate into heightened mission readiness and response capabilities.The meeting also witnessed the presentation of the National Maritime Search & Rescue Awards 2026, recognising exemplary efforts in saving lives at sea.

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has approved revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Utilisation of MoD Proof Ranges, Field Firing Ranges & Test Facilities by Indian Defence Industry. The revised SOP provides for a detailed and simplified procedure for allotment and utilisation of MoD proof ranges and laboratory testing facilities, along with requisite formats.
The key features of the revised SOP are as follows:
Proof/testing charges have been waived for iDEX, TDF, Make and other developmental projects of the Ministry of Defence, to promote ‘Atmanirbharta in Defence’.
The SOP lists the Proof Ranges, Field Firing Ranges and Laboratory Test Facilities available with DRDO, Government Quality Assurance agencies and the three Services for utilisation by the Indian defence industry.
The procedure for calculation and payment of proof/testing charges, wherever applicable, has been incorporated in the SOP, thereby simplifying the documentation and process for industry.
The provision for Arbitration in the existing SOP has been replaced with a simpler and industry-friendly Conciliation Agreement Clause, to facilitate Ease of Doing Business through faster resolution of issues faced by the indigenous defence industry.
A three-day slot per quarter has been reserved at Proof Ranges for proof firing of developmental projects sponsored by the Government, including iDEX, TDF, Make and other developmental projects of the Ministry of Defence, as well as developmental projects undertaken under the own initiative of the indigenous defence industry.
The revised SOP aims to provide simpler, transparent and industry-friendly access to proof ranges, field firing ranges and test facilities. It incorporates various Government initiatives aimed at facilitating indigenisation, innovation and defence exports, besides providing proof and test support to developmental projects undertaken by the Indian defence industry.

title: COP31 should focus on Closing Gaps, Fulfilling Commitments and Accelerating Implementation of Paris Agreement, stresses India
subtitle: Measure Success in Antalya by Accelerated Implementation, Support reaching those in Need and Scaling up existing Solutions: Shri Bhupender Yadav
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 OCT 2026 8:17AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav addressing the plenary discussion on COP31 priorities at the UNFCCC Pre-COP31 meeting in Fiji today, called for greater focus on closing gaps in understanding, fulfilling existing climate commitments and accelerating implementation of the Paris Agreement. He is leading the Indian Delegation at the UNFCCC’s Pre-COP31 meeting being co-hosted by Australia, Fiji and Tuvalu.
Beginning his intervention, Shri Yadav saluted the spirit of the people of Tuvalu for “bravely combating the challenges of climate change” and setting an example of a successful model. He said that their efforts strengthen hope, confidence and the resolve to stand united in combating climate change.
The Minister said that the long-term objectives and goals have already been established under the UNFCCC and its Paris Agreement, including the ambition of limiting global temperature rise to 1.5°C. He emphasised that achieving this ambition would require commensurate means of implementation and that the focus now should be on assessing how the world can accelerate its journey towards these goals.
Referring to the COP31 Presidencies’ focus on consensus, decision-making and implementation, Shri Yadav said there is an overall
Consensus
on the long-term goals and direction of climate multilateralism. However, there is a need to identify and develop consensus on existing gaps in understanding, including gaps between science and traditional knowledge and community practices, between practices and ethics, and between available resources and felt needs. The Minister said that COP31 should endeavour to close these gaps in understanding.
On
Decision-making
, Shri Yadav said the key decision required from Parties is to fulfil their commitments under the UNFCCC and the Paris Agreement “in true letter and spirit” and enable each Party to fulfil these commitments. On
Implementation
, the Minister called for addressing identified gaps where the need is highest and the impact is visible and felt by the majority. He emphasised the need for greater capacity building and urged Parties to bring concrete examples and success stories every year—demonstrating high-impact mitigation, large-scale adaptation and effective delivery of means of implementation.
Shri Yadav said that consistently sharing and scaling such examples year after year would yield better results on the ground in achieving the goals of the Paris Agreement. He concluded that success in Antalya should not be measured simply by new targets or declarations, but by whether implementation is accelerated, support reaches those who need it, and existing solutions can be taken to scale.
The Pre-COP is a preparatory meeting held a few weeks before the annual UN Climate Change Conference, which this year will be held in Antalya, Türkiye, in November.

title: Adopted Joint Statement after the India-UK Financial Markets Dialogue 2026, held in London
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 OCT 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The fourth UK-India Financial Markets Dialogue (FMD) took place on 29th September 2026 in London. The Dialogue was led by senior officials from the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, and HM Treasury, with participation from Indian and UK financial services regulatory authorities, including the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA), the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) and the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) the Bank of England (BoE) and the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA).
The Dialogue opened with reflections on developments since the previous meeting in December 2024. Participants exchanged updates on reforms in their respective jurisdictions and reaffirmed their shared ambition for sustainable economic growth, resilient and open financial markets, and increased bilateral trade and investment. Discussions focused on capital markets, insurance and pensions, asset management, and fintech. Both sides welcomed ongoing regulatory engagement and the role of the India-UK Financial Partnership (IUKFP) in supporting practical cooperation between policymakers, regulators and industry in areas such as Fintech, AI, green and sustainable finance, and asset management.
Capital markets
Participants exchanged updates on respective capital markets reforms. On the Indian side, SEBI shared how India is transforming global investor participation by streamlining market entry and operations and RBI highlighted the significant ease of overseas access to sovereign and corporate debt. They discussed the growing role of Gujarat International Finance Tec-City International Financial Services Centre (GIFT IFSC) in mobilising international capital into India and agreed to continue regulatory cooperation and knowledge-sharing to support GIFT IFSC’s development as an international financial centre.
Participants discussed opportunities to increase cross-border investment and Indian firms’ access to international capital including through cross-border equity and bond listings via GIFT-IFSC, and stronger capital market connectivity. Both sides agreed to identify priority areas to explore for future capital markets cooperation ahead of the next Economic and Financial Dialogue.
Insurance and pensions
Participants discussed their respective insurance and pensions reforms and market opportunities. The UK outlined recent updates to its insurance regulatory framework as part of the Financial Services Growth and Competitiveness Strategy and developments in its pensions and annuity markets, while India outlined its ambitions to expand coverage, investment and market capacity. To support market development, bilateral trade and investment, both sides agreed on the importance of the Insurance and Pensions Workplan established in 2023.
Participants recognised the value of competitive and resilient markets, access to specialist expertise, diverse pools of capital and reinsurance capacity in managing complex risks and supporting long-term domestic development. Both sides discussed the opportunities in reinsurance arising from India’s evolving regulatory framework, and from deeper cooperation between the London Market and Indian insurers and reinsurers.
Participants also exchanged experiences in pensions regulation, governance, coverage and long-term savings reform. They discussed measures to increase participation and support productive long-term investment, and agreed to explore knowledge sharing in areas aligned with their domestic priorities.
Regulatory cooperation: Asset management and sustainable finance
The UK and India exchanged updates on asset management regulation and markets. The UK set out work on the regulatory framework for alternative investment fund managers. India provided an overview of the key reforms undertaken by SEBI and IFSCA across their respective regulatory frameworks. Both sides welcomed continued regulatory cooperation on asset management and discussed how mutual understanding of reforms, investor requirements and market conditions could support increased cross-border investment.
Both sides welcomed further internationalisation of the Indian rupee and recognised London’s role as the leading offshore rupee trading hub. On sustainable finance, t
hey discussed the importance of credible sustainable finance frameworks, high-quality disclosures, global standards and investor confidence in mobilising private capital for the low-carbon and climate-resilient transition.
Participants reviewed progress under the IUKFP asset management workstream and recognised the value of industry evidence in identifying practical opportunities for deeper participation by UK and Indian asset managers in each other’s markets.
Fintech and Innovation
Participants exchanged updates on their respective approaches to fintech and innovation. India shared its experience on scaling fintech adoption and financial inclusion, through digital public infrastructure (DPI), including digital identity, digital payments, Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs) and data exchange frameworks.
Both sides agreed the importance of supporting responsible innovation and competition without compromising regulatory oversight.
Both sides exchanged perspectives on the potential opportunities and risks of artificial intelligence (AI) in financial services and agreed on the value of continued bilateral exchange and coordination through relevant international fora. India shared its digital onboarding process for retail financial services and committed to further share its experiences. Both sides also noted the risks posed by criminal adoption of new technologies to financial crime, including use of AI to commit fraud at industrial scale in so-called ‘scam compounds’ operating in foreign countries as well as risks to cyber security, data protection and operational resilience. Participants shared experience of using technology and regulatory innovation to detect and prevent financial fraud, and agreed to continue cooperation between the relevant authorities.
Both sides reaffirmed their support for the G20 Roadmap for Enhancing Cross-Border Payments. They discussed practical priorities for reducing frictions, improving transparency and facilitating greater efficiency in cross-border payments aligned to the G20 Roadmap.
Both sides updated on developments relating to their retail payment infrastructures, and recognised the work at the G20 to continue to promote interoperability and interlinkages of electronic payment infrastructures.
Future cooperation
The UK and India welcomed the constructive discussions and reaffirmed the important role of the FMD in supporting their shared ambitions for sustainable growth, deeper trade and investment, and resilient financial markets. Both sides welcomed the contribution of the IUKFP in identifying practical and potential solutions to deepen financial services links. Both sides reflected on a strengthened relationship particularly in the context of the launch of Vision 2035, and the importance of driving the implementation of the UK-India Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) which entered into force on 15 July 2026.
Participants agreed to drive progress across the workstreams, with updates reviewed through the relevant bilateral mechanisms and at the next UK-India Economic and Financial Dialogue.

at Malana village in Kullu district, Himachal Pradesh, on October 6, 2026, as part of its Preventive Outreach under
Yuva Raksha
initiatives and efforts towards fulfilling CBN’s mandate to promoting alternative development in illicit cannabis cultivation affected areas as per India's National Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) policy, 2012 and Vision document on Narcotics Control 2026–2029.

Nasha Mukt Bharat

Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan
through sustained preventive awareness, youth engagement and community participation.

Jan Samvad
initiative, the
Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN)
conducted awareness drives to sensitize rural youth and populations on the harmful impacts of
cannabis (
ganja
)
,
charas
, and
hashish oil
consumption. Concurrently, the CBN actively encouraged villagers to adopt
alternative development and cropping systems

title: National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP) notifies regulations for autonomous boards and central assessment committee to strengthen quality, transparency and standardisation in allied and healthcare education
subtitle:
Autonomous Boards to strengthen quality assessment and standards in allied and healthcare institutions

NCAHP notifies competency based Diploma in Medical Radiology and Imaging Technology curriculum under One Nation One Curriculum

Two-year D.MRIT programme to include six-month clinical internship in radiology and imaging

NCAHP introduces digital registration with Unique Identification numbers and QR-coded certificates for allied and healthcare professionals

State and Central Registers to enable public verification of allied and healthcare professionals
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 OCT 2026 6:49PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, has notified measures under the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act, 2021 to strengthen standards in allied and healthcare education and professional practice. These include the Autonomous Boards and Central Assessment Committee (Establishment, Constitution, Functions and Powers) Regulations, 2026, the competency-based curriculum for the Diploma in Medical Radiology and Imaging Technology (D.MRIT) and the Registration of Allied and Healthcare Professionals Regulations, 2026.
The measures provide for institutional assessment and quality assurance, competency-based education and training and a structured system for registration and verification of allied and healthcare professionals.
Strengthening institutional standards through Autonomous Boards and Central Assessment Committee
The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP) has notified the following regulations – (a) Registration of Allied and Healthcare Professionals Regulations, 2026 (b) Autonomous Boards and Central Assessment Committee (Establishment, Constitution, Functions and Powers) Regulations, 2026, under the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act, 2021. The Regulations provide a framework for strengthening institutional assessment, quality assurance and implementation of standards for recognised courses.
Salient Features of the Regulations
The Regulations provide for the establishment and functioning of Autonomous Boards under State Allied and Healthcare Councils, with defined responsibilities for education, institutional assessment, professional ethics and registration. The Autonomous Boards will have 10 to 20 members, including a President, with representation from recognised allied and healthcare professional categories.
The Undergraduate and Postgraduate Boards will facilitate implementation of standards for recognised courses, competency-based frameworks, faculty development, training and research, and will submit reports and recommendations to the State Council.
The Assessment and Rating Board will evaluate applications for recognition and Letters of Permission, undertake institutional inspections, review annual disclosures, empanel assessors, assess and rate institutions, and make assessment and rating information available in the public domain through the State Council website.
The Ethics and Registration Board will verify the documents of professionals and recommend for registration. The Board will support the maintenance of the State registers and the implementation of professional ethics and conduct standards, and will evaluate complaints and violations and make recommendations concerning professional registration.
Central Assessment Committee (CAC)
For States where a functional State Council does not exist, the Regulations provide for a Central Assessment Committee (CAC) under the overall supervision of NCAHP and assisted by the NCAHP Secretariat. The CAC will perform the functions of Autonomous Boards and follow the prescribed verification, inspection and rating procedures.
The CAC will comprise 10 to 30 members, including a President, with representation from professional categories and additional representation, where required, to ensure appropriate State and Union Territory coverage, particularly for areas without functional State Councils.
The Regulations also prescribe grounds and due process for removal of CAC members, including conflict of interest, breach of code, abuse of position and other specified circumstances, with an opportunity of hearing.
Towards Standardised and Quality driven Allied and Healthcare Education
The NCAHP had previously notified the Registration of Allied and Healthcare Professionals Regulations, 2026, enabling allied and healthcare professionals to register under the Act and practice their profession. The notification of these regulations ensures a seamless and transparent registration process in Central and State registers.
By establishing clearly defined institutional assessment, inspection and rating mechanisms, together with dedicated functions for education, ethics and registration, the Regulations provide a structured framework for improving the quality of education and professional standards in the allied and healthcare sector.
Competency-based education to meet growing demand for trained imaging professionals
With the objective of standardising education and training, NCAHP has notified the competency-based curriculum for the Diploma in Medical Radiology and Imaging Technology (D.MRIT) on 30th September 2026 under One Nation One Curriculum for the Allied and Healthcare sector.
Institutions imparting or intending to impart the D.MRIT course must mandatorily adopt the curriculum from the academic year 2027–28. Institutes desiring to implement it during the academic year 2026–27 may adopt the curriculum from that academic year.
The Diploma programme has been developed keeping in view the growing requirement for trained professionals in Medical Radiology and Imaging services at Primary Health Centres (PHCs), hospitals, diagnostic centres and other healthcare facilities. There has also been demand from students and stakeholders for an appropriate diploma-level programme in the field of Radiology and Imaging.
The D.MRIT is a two-year programme for students who have completed Class 12 in the Science stream with Physics, Chemistry and Biology (PCB) from a recognised Board or equivalent. The curriculum represents a transition from traditional, knowledge-oriented education towards a competency-based approach, with emphasis on the acquisition of Knowledge, Skills, Values and Attitudes required for safe, effective and ethical practice in Medical Radiology and Imaging services.
An important component of the programme is a six-month internship, designed to provide students with structured hands-on clinical exposure and opportunities to apply theoretical knowledge in real-world healthcare settings. The internship will facilitate the development of practical skills, professional competencies, patient-care practices, radiation safety practices and familiarity with imaging procedures and equipment under appropriate supervision.
The curriculum is designed to ensure that professionals completing the programme acquire the requisite theoretical knowledge, practical skills and professional competencies to function in Medical Radiology and Imaging and contribute effectively to diagnostic services such as X-rays, CT Scan, Sonography, Mammography and Fluoroscopy, while adhering to prescribed standards of patient safety, radiation protection, quality assurance and professional practice.
The notification of the Diploma programme complements the competency-based education framework already established by the Commission for higher levels of education in the discipline. The Bachelor of Medical Radiology and Imaging Technology (B.MRIT) and Master of Medical Radiology and Imaging Technology (M.MRIT) competency-based curricula were earlier released by the Commission vide notice dated 24th April 2025, for implementation from the academic year 2026–27.
The introduction of the D.MRIT curriculum alongside the existing Bachelor’s and Master’s programmes provides a structured educational pathway in Medical Radiology and Imaging Technology and is aimed at supporting the availability of appropriately trained professionals while promoting uniformity, standardisation and quality in Allied and Healthcare education across the country.
The Commission has so far released 20 competency-based curricula across various Allied and Healthcare Professions. These curricula have been developed with the objective of strengthening competency-based education, standardising training and ensuring that students acquire the knowledge, skills and professional attributes required for contemporary healthcare delivery.
Registration framework to strengthen transparency and verification of professionals
The Registration of Allied and Healthcare Professionals Regulations, 2026, notified by NCAHP and published in the Gazette of India on 15th September 2026, establish a comprehensive framework for registration of allied and healthcare professionals in both the State Registers and the Central Register, along with issuance of certificates of registration with Unique Identification (UID) numbers through an online system.
A person will be entitled to practise a recognised allied and healthcare profession only after obtaining registration in accordance with the Regulations. Eligibility requires holding a recognised primary qualification. Professionals residing in a State or Union Territory where a functional State Council has not yet been established may register directly with the Central Register.
Registration will remain valid for five years and may be renewed upon fulfilment of Continuing Professional Development (CPD) requirements through approved online and offline modes.
The Regulations provide for real-time synchronisation between the State Registers and the Central Register through an integrated online system. The Central and State Registers will be accessible to the public through the websites of the Commission and the respective State Councils, displaying prescribed particulars of registered professionals and enabling verification of registration status.
Every registered professional will be issued a Unique Identification (UID) number through the centralised system. Registration certificates, including digital certificates featuring the UID and a secure QR code, will be issued by the Commission or the respective State Council, facilitating identification and verification of registered professionals.
The Regulations also provide for interim registration for students enrolled in recognised institutions who are undertaking internships, clinical training, observerships or practical coursework required to complete an allied and healthcare qualification. Interim registration must be initiated by the recognised institution and obtained from the concerned State Council, with no fee charged for interim registration applications.
The Regulations establish a pathway for Indian citizens holding foreign qualifications in allied and healthcare. A foreign-qualified allied and healthcare professional will be eligible to apply for registration where the qualification is recognised by the Commission or the prescribed credential equivalency evaluation has been completed, along with the relevant exit examination where applicable. Temporary registration is also provided for eligible foreign-qualified Indian professionals for specific, time-bound purposes including postgraduate or specialty education, fellowships, clinical research, observerships, advanced workshops, expert visits and voluntary community service.
The Regulations permit temporary registration for sponsored foreign professionals for specific, timebound purposes. They also provide for Good Standing Certificates for registered allied and healthcare professionals pursuing foreign education, carrying out professional activities or participating in student exchange programmes outside India.
The Commission is undertaking efforts to introduce provisional registration for professionals currently practising in the allied and healthcare sector who lack the prescribed primary qualifications. Such professionals will be provided an option to undergo a bridge course to attain eligibility for regular registration.
The registration and payment of fee will be processed through an online portal, supporting a more streamlined registration process and greater transparency in the allied and healthcare workforce.
Taken together, these measures strengthen standards in allied and healthcare education and professional practice through institutional assessment, competency-based training and a transparent system of professional registration and verification.
The framework seeks to support quality education and training and enable patients and service users to verify the registration of allied and healthcare professionals.

title: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda to Lead National Launch of JOSH Teams Tomorrow at Bharat Mandapam
subtitle:
Union Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Minister of State for Defence Shri Sanjay Seth and Delhi Chief Minister Smt. Rekha Gupta to Join National Launch of JOSH Teams

JOSH Teams to be Rolled Out Across 55 Districts in 11 States in First Phase to Strengthen Youth-Led Community Mobilisation for TB Mukt Bharat

JOSH Teams to take TB Mukt Bharat Message to Grassroots; Class-I Officers, MY Bharat Volunteers and NCC Cadets to Drive Community Engagement

JOSH Teams to Strengthen Grassroots Participation in India’s TB Elimination Efforts, building on 67,933 Panchayats Across 697 Districts Recognised as TB Mukt in 2025

Initiative Reflects Whole-of-Government and Whole-of-Society Approach by Bringing Together Health, Youth and Defence Networks in the Fight Against TB
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 OCT 2026 10:05AM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a significant step towards further strengthening community participation in India’s fight against tuberculosis (TB), the Union Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, in collaboration with the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports and the Ministry of Defence, will launch
JOSH (Joint Squad for Health) Teams
on
8 October 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi
. In the first phase, JOSH Teams will be rolled out across
55 districts in 11 States
, with the objective of strengthening youth-led community mobilisation and taking the message of
TB Mukt Bharat
to the grassroots.
Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare and Chemicals & Fertilizers, Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, will lead the national launch of JOSH Teams in the presence of Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Union Minister for Labour & Employment and Youth Affairs & Sports; Shri Sanjay Seth, Minister of State for Defence; and Smt. Rekha Gupta, Chief Minister of Delhi. The event will bring together senior leadership and stakeholders from the participating Ministries, elected representatives, Class-I Officers, MY Bharat Volunteers, NCC Cadets and other stakeholders associated with India’s TB elimination efforts.
The programme will feature an achievement video highlighting key milestones of the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, followed by the formal launch of JOSH Teams. New Information, Education and Communication (IEC) materials for the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan will also be launched. The event will further witness the launch of Khushi Avatar, an AI-powered chatbot, aimed at strengthening public awareness, community engagement and participation in the national effort towards TB elimination.
Structured Youth Participation for Grassroots TB Mobilisation
JOSH Teams have been envisaged as a structured mechanism to translate the energy and reach of India’s youth into organised community action for TB elimination. The teams will bring together Class-I Officers, MY Bharat Volunteers and NCC Cadets, combining administrative leadership with the extensive youth networks and community outreach capabilities of MY Bharat and NCC.
In the first phase, the initiative will focus on strengthening engagement at the Block/Ward and community levels, taking the TB Mukt Bharat message beyond health facilities and closer to people and communities where they live, work and interact.
Through community outreach and engagement, JOSH Teams will support the dissemination of key messages on TB symptoms, prevention, timely diagnosis and completion of treatment. They will also contribute to efforts to address myths and misconceptions surrounding TB, reduce stigma and encourage individuals, families and communities to participate actively in the national TB elimination movement.
The initiative seeks to enable young people to become active partners in the TB response, providing them with a defined platform to contribute to awareness generation, social mobilisation and community engagement. The convergence of Class-I Officers, MY Bharat Volunteers and NCC Cadets will further strengthen the connect between government programmes and communities at the grassroots.
Building on the Power of Jan Bhagidari
The JOSH Teams initiative builds on the growing emphasis on community participation and Jan Bhagidari as important pillars of India’s TB elimination efforts. In 2025, 67,933 Panchayats across 697 districts were recognised as TB Mukt, reflecting the collective efforts of health workers, elected representatives, community members and volunteers in advancing the national TB elimination agenda.
This achievement underscores the importance of local leadership, community ownership and sustained participation in taking the TB elimination message to the last mile. JOSH Teams will build on this spirit of Jan Bhagidari by harnessing the energy, outreach and social networks of young people to further strengthen awareness, mobilisation and community participation in the TB response.
Whole-of-Government, Whole-of-Society Approach
JOSH Teams represent the Government’s whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach to TB elimination by bringing together the institutional strengths and outreach networks of the health, youth and defence sectors.
The Union Ministry of Health & Family Welfare will provide the overall public health and TB elimination framework, while the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports and the Ministry of Defence will facilitate the participation of MY Bharat Volunteers and NCC Cadets, respectively, in community-level mobilisation and outreach.
The initiative reflects the Government’s continued emphasis on convergence across Ministries and sectors, enabling diverse institutional and community networks to contribute towards a common national goal.
The launch of JOSH Teams marks another important step in the Government’s efforts to build a people-centred, participatory and community-driven response to TB, with coordinated action involving Ministries, States and Union Territories, health workers, elected representatives, youth and citizens.
Through stronger grassroots engagement and greater Jan Bhagidari, JOSH Teams will further reinforce the collective resolve to build a TB Mukt Bharat.

title: Four AI-enabled films unveiled under IICT-YouTube collaborative ‘Create with AI’ programme
subtitle: IICT advances India’s AI filmmaking ecosystem through technology, mentorship and creative innovation
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 OCT 2026 7:03PM by PIB Mumbai
content:
Mumbai : 7 October 2026
The Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT) and YouTube are marking a key milestone in the Create with AI programme, announced in November 2025 to support AI-led creative projects and strengthen India’s capabilities in emerging technologies. The programme has now debuted its first four AI-enabled short films, marking a step towards building an ecosystem that can position India as a global leader in AI-led filmmaking.
The four films unveiled at the IICT Theatre in Mumbai today, were also released by the filmmakers on their YouTube channels at the same time. These
films showcase a diverse range of subjects and storytelling approaches, spanning history, mythology, human emotion and space exploration, while demonstrating the creative possibilities of AI-enabled filmmaking.
‘Chekavar’
by Avium Studios is a fictional cinematic story set against the historic Battle of Colachel in 1741, drawing inspiration from the land, people, courage and martial traditions of the era.
‘CHANAKYA – The Mind of an Empire’
by Eleventh Door Studio is a historical epic exploring the untold journey of Chanakya, the philosopher, strategist and architect of the Mauryan Empire.
‘DEVI: The Nine Astras
’ by Kalpanik Films portrays the divine manifestation of Shakti and her epic battle to restore cosmic balance.
‘Laika by Karthik Kult Kreations’
shows the emotional journey of a dog sent into space, exploring themes of courage, sacrifice and the bond between humans and animals against the backdrop of space exploration.
These films demonstrate that AI is most powerful when it expands creative possibilities while the filmmaker remains firmly at the centre of the storytelling process. The Create with AI programme was designed as a hands-on experiment to bring together Google and YouTube’s AI technologies, IICT’s infrastructure and faculty mentorship, and the imagination of filmmakers.
Speaking on the occasion, CEO, IICT, Dr. Vishwas Deoskar said, India has the opportunity to lead the next chapter of AI-led filmmaking. The Create with AI programme brings together institutional mentorship and access to advanced AI tools, giving Indian creative studios the opportunity to experiment, build capabilities and develop new filmmaking workflows. This is an important step towards creating an ecosystem that can place India at the forefront of AI-driven storytelling, he added.
Highlighting the potential of generative AI for creators, Managing Director, YouTube India, Ms Gunjan Soni said, India has always been an extraordinary storytelling nation, but we are now seeing independent creators build production powerhouses on their own terms. “Our partnership with IICT demonstrates what happens when fearless Indian storytelling meets frontier technology to produce world-class cinema on an independent scale”, she stated.
The dignitaries present on the occasion included the senior officers of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, including Director General (West Zone), Ms Smita Vats Sharma; Joint Secretary, Minstry of I & B, Shri Senthil Rajan; MD of NFDC, Shri Prakash Magdum and CEO of CBFC, Shri Rajendra Singh.
Please scan the link below for more details on the AI movies showcased in the event.
Generative AI fundamentally removes production bottlenecks, thereby giving creators valuable time back to focus on writing, world-building, and craft.
According to a new Gen Media India report by Public First and Google, generative media tools offer a 20% productivity boost for creative workers in India. That translates to saving roughly 390 hours every year, effectively giving creators nearly ten full weeks back just to focus on writing, world-building, and refining their craft.
About IICT:
The Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT) is India’s National Centre of Excellence for Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics and Extended Reality (AVGC-XR), established with the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, Government of India, Government of Maharashtra, FICCI and CII. Its first campus began functioning at the NFDC Complex in July 2025, while a permanent 10-acre campus is being developed at Film City, Goregaon. IICT currently offers 18 courses and has partnerships with leading global technology and media companies.

title: 5th Meeting of Live Events Development Cell Reviews Single-Window Clearances and Next-Gen Reforms for Live Events Sector
subtitle:
India’s Live Events Sector Grows 44% in One Year, Supports Over One Crore Livelihoods

Government Targets Doubling of Live Events Sector by 2030 through Centre-State-Industry Collaboration

States and UTs Urged to Route End-to-End Live Event Licensing through India Cine Hub Portal

Single National Music Licence, Notified Entertainment Zones and Infrastructure Status for Live Event Venues Discussed
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 OCT 2026 6:24PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, Shri Chanchal Kumar, said today that India’s live events sector grew by
44 per cent over the past year
, with around
34,000 events
held across the country and the sector now supporting more than
one crore livelihoods
. Addressing the 5th meeting of the Live Events Development Cell (LEDC), he said the Government has set an ambitious target of
doubling the sector by 2030
, with the potential to generate
15–20 million direct and ancillary jobs
. He described the LEDC as
“one of the finest examples of cooperation between industry, States and the Centre”.
Shri Chanchal Kumar highlighted the LEDC brings together
14 Central Ministries and Departments, 10 States and UTs and 21 industry bodies
, and has taken forward key reforms including the
Model Executive Order, Single Window Portal on India Cine Hub, streamlined clearances and skilling initiatives
. He noted that the number of States and UTs with designated Nodal Officers has increased from
16 to 29
.
The meeting reviewed the implementation of the Single Window Clearances Portal for the live event industry on the India Cine Hub (ICH) portal. States and UTs were asked to designate Nodal Officers, nominate authorised officers from departments, integrate departmental and local licensing systems with the ICH Portal,
route the complete licence lifecycle through the portal
, onboard live event venues and notify live event licensing as a time-bound public service.
Further, it was informed that
five States
have so far adopted the
“Model Executive Order for Streamlining Licensing and Permissions for Live Events in India, 2026”
, which was shared with States and Union Territories on 13th March 2026. The state of Maharashtra, (LEDC member State) has adopted the MEO and made a presentation on its implementation. The remaining States and Union Territories were urged to expedite adoption. It was also informed that the Ministry of Home Affairs has streamlined FRRO re-registration requirements for short-term stays by foreign performers.
Central Ministries were requested to take forward sector-specific facilitation, including group visa provisions for artists and crews with customs duty exemption for show equipment by the concerned ministries; integration of live entertainment skills into the National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF), training and certification centres and apprenticeship programmes by the Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship; promotion of India as a global hub for
event-based tourism
by the Ministry of Tourism; and financial incentives including
GST rationalisation
and CSR alignment, infrastructure financing through VGF and blended finance, and recognition of the live entertainment sector under MSME by the respective ministries.
Further, the LEDC deliberated on next-generation reforms, including a
single national music licence
with notified tariffs to replace overlapping demands from multiple rights societies, notified entertainment precincts under the Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000, and relaxation of caps on foreign remittances for payments to international artists.
On pre-approved venues, it was informed that the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) and the Sports Authority of India (SAI) have issued SOPs for organising live events at their assets, and major venues are to be pre-approved so that organisers need not seek the same venue-level permissions for each event.
The LEDC further reviewed the framework for “Brownfield and Greenfield Venue Development” to address the shortage of purpose-built venues. State Governments, industry stakeholders and sports authorities were requested to provide their formal feedback on the draft framework. Proposals discussed include identification and development of purpose-built venues by States, inclusion of live event and performance venues above a threshold capacity in the
Harmonised Master List of Infrastructure Sub-sectors
, and project support through the
Viability Gap Funding
scheme.
The Live Event Skilling Committee, chaired by the Vice Chancellor, Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC), presented the progress on the skilling curriculum, including the
MoU between IIMC, MESC and EEMA
, and certificate and short-term courses in live events. Stakeholders were encouraged to adopt these modules through their skilling institutions. It was also proposed that
Inclusivity Guidelines for Safety of Women and Divyang-jan at Live Events and Concerts
and a
Green Concert Protocol
be launched at
WAVES 2027
with the support of the industry.
The meeting concluded with the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting reaffirming its commitment to working closely with all stakeholders to foster a supportive and growth-oriented ecosystem for India's live events sector.
